metadata.title: SOPP 8001.6 Procedures for Parallel Scientific Advice with European Medicines Agency (EMA)
metadata.edition: 8001.6 · listed on the FDA SOPP page, 2026-11-26
metadata.legal_basis: CBER Standard Operating Procedure and Policy (internal FDA procedure). Informative; not binding on applicants.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.
Candidates are not approved requirements. Read the original, qualifications and exceptions.
Scans, tables, other languages and implicit obligations may be missed. Zero candidates does not establish zero requirements.

candidates.statement: B. The PSA should focus primarily on specific questions or issues involving the development of an eligible product for which the sponsor desires to have further scientific input from both EMA and FDA.
candidates.context: A. The PSA process is voluntary and initiated at the sponsor’s request. A PSA may be suggested to the sponsor by either the EMA or FDA as a possible mechanism for interaction. C. A PSA is intended to address a single set of questions submitted by a sponsor and should not be viewed as an ongoing series of consultations.

candidates.statement: C. A PSA is intended to address a single set of questions submitted by a sponsor and should not be viewed as an ongoing series of consultations.
candidates.context: B. The PSA should focus primarily on specific questions or issues involving the development of an eligible product for which the sponsor desires to have further scientific input from both EMA and FDA. D. The PSA takes place under the provisions of the confidentiality commitments between the FDA and EMA and with the sponsor’s authorization.

candidates.statement: E. Each agency will provide, according to its usual procedures, independent advice to the sponsor on the questions posed during the PSA. Sponsors should not expect to receive the same recommendations from both agencies regarding product development issues or marketing applications that have undergone PSA.
candidates.context: D. The PSA takes place under the provisions of the confidentiality commitments between the FDA and EMA and with the sponsor’s authorization. While a potential beneficial outcome of PSA is increased convergence of advice, the two agencies’ advice may differ. It is anticipated that following a PSA, sponsors should have a clearer understanding of the agencies’ respective requirements and perspectives with regard to the development program discussed, and, if divergent, the reasons for the divergence.

candidates.context: E. Each agency will provide, according to its usual procedures, independent advice to the sponsor on the questions posed during the PSA. Sponsors should not expect to receive the same recommendations from both agencies regarding product development issues or marketing applications that have undergone PSA. F. Both agencies remain committed to meeting domestic process and review goals and timeframes. As envisioned, the PSA procedures should not adversely affect either agency’s ability to meet formal domestic performance expectations.

candidates.statement: F. Both agencies remain committed to meeting domestic process and review goals and timeframes. As envisioned, the PSA procedures should not adversely affect either agency’s ability to meet formal domestic performance expectations.

Therefore, each agency shall be cognizant of the other’s formal domestic performance expectations and be as flexible as possible in scheduling PSA meetings to fulfill those requirements.

H. The relevant CBER product office will have a “PSA Product Office Lead” who is responsible for coordinating the PSA per office procedure. An office may choose to have an established designated lead, or to identify a specific lead with each request.

candidates.statement: I. If the CBER product office is contacted directly by the sponsor, the product office should notify the CBER Associate Director for International Affairs (ADIA), and the ADIA will undertake further appropriate communication.

candidates.statement: L. Meetings with the SAWP will need to be held on dates that conform to its schedule. The CBER Foreign Regulatory Communications Coordinator (FRCC) will provide the SAWP calendar to the product office PSA Lead to facilitate scheduling. In addition, due to time differences, meetings with the SAWP must start between 8:00 a.m. and 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time.
candidates.context: 3. The concluding meeting between the SAWP, the FDA, and the sponsor after which the scientific advice is provided according to each agency’s process timelines. M. CBER staff making reference in a review to any non-public information shared by foreign government officials under FDA’s confidentiality commitments must provide appropriate reference information in the review such that future readers know the source of information is confidential. The source document or information itself should not be included in the review file, but rather a memorandum should be included which states the document or information was shared under FDA’s confidentiality commitments. The memorandum should include the date the source document or information was shared and state that the document is archived in the CBER International Affairs SharePoint site.
